findings.title: A review with a different approved base can clear the current unit blocker
findings.diagnosis: review-packet accepts caller-selected repository_root and base_revision, and derives artifact_digest when the caller omits it. corePacketState checks active route and accepted plan, but never compares this base with the core approval BaseRevisionDigest or establishes that the root belongs to that approved repository. A nonce-bound receipt/report then proves consistency with this wrongly selected packet. findings-import treats that APPROVE as sufficient to replace the current unit findings. Two independent reproductions clear A-only-blocker: base changed to HEAD in the same root, and another root/base. No receipt rewriting, same-UID adversary, core tampering or manual provenance override is needed after the synthetic approved fixture is created through transition.Apply. This violates architecture §§6 and 7.1 and leaves prior F04 only partly closed. The reproduction demonstrates blocker removal and host APPROVE, not an authentic human stage transition or verified closure.

evidence.observation: Independent -race reproduction has two failures and two valid controls. A same-root changed base and a different repository/base each obtain APPROVE and an empty finding snapshot that removes A-only-blocker. Current approved-base control succeeds; explicitly supplying A artifact against B refuses. Core chain was generated through four ordinary transition.Apply edges with clearly labelled synthetic approvals.

Packet computes target from caller-selected root/base and allows omitted artifact_digest. corePacketState checks route/plan but does not compare packet base to active core approval base. Import rechecks live state against that packet, not against core approved repository/base.
Core approved base 10db4b7ce8ce827346b7154577f5df433f776e3a; packet reviewed base 9a67b66cd64fcbf5dfd59a30375969850ed017cd. Final core record is findings_snapshot:true with no findings.
Core approved base 709a82c423c5b66d813e3f5a42a8bd4b741c6cfb; packet reviewed base 8d26faccfe597c262277cccf32342500593ca52e. Final core record removes A-only-blocker.

fix.action: Before writing a usable packet or dispatch, resolve the unit's active core approval and require packet BaseRevision to equal its BaseRevisionDigest. Bind the canonical repository root/identity to the run from authoritative grounding rather than from this review request; refuse findings resolution if this association is unavailable or differs. Carry these bindings in the fixed packet and recheck them under the existing locks at dispatch, review-import and findings-import. Do not let omitted artifact_digest substitute a new approved repository/base. Preserve the legacy compatibility label and require explicit migration of records lacking the authoritative association.
fix.why: Nonce, receipt and live-target equality currently establish only packet self-consistency. They do not establish that the packet reviews the repository/base whose findings it may resolve. The existing approved base is already available without the deferred Gate D acceptance contract.

verification.method: Run TestAuditor7OtherRepositoryCannotResolveCurrentRun under -race with the ordinary transition.Apply fixture. Fingerprint core/host chains before the changed-base and different-repository requests.
verification.expected: Both negative requests refuse before dispatch/approval/snapshot append; A-only-blocker remains; the exact current-base control still imports and resolves only its unit.

verification.method: Retest explicit artifact mismatch, unchanged target, dirty target, same-base other-repository association, and legacy records without canonical association.
verification.expected: Wrong repository/base never obtains resolution authority, even with omitted artifact_digest; valid exact targets still work; unsupported legacy association fails closed with visible migration guidance.

verification.method: Rerun go test, go vet, -race and host-dogfood with independent audit of the exact repaired diff.
verification.expected: All existing Gate B/C controls pass; no stage advances without a new bound human approval.

fix.tradeoffs: This may refuse old packet-generation callers that selected another base or lack a recorded authoritative root. Migration must preserve old chain bytes and all findings/waivers. The smallest containment is approved-base comparison; that alone cannot prove repository identity when unrelated roots share a base commit.
fix.alternative: Require a separately authoritative target association before enabling findings resolution, and keep all current blockers while this binding is missing. A mandatory caller artifact digest provides additional drift detection but is insufficient by itself if the same caller can choose both root and digest.

findings.priority: Repair before Gate C acceptance; then independently re-audit the exact target.
findings.root_cause_confidence: observed missing comparison; broader repository association remedy remains proposed

prior_findings.assessment: Contract-dependent full packet inputs are explicitly moved to Gate D. In-scope current core head/plan/route/findings/waivers are present and core drift checks remain.

prior_findings.assessment: Baseline-written record loads byte-identically, own finding can resolve, active waiver remains, and ambiguous source owner stays unowned.

prior_findings.assessment: Legacy and migrated enforcement labels are explicit; migrated manual overrides refuse.

prior_findings.assessment: New unanswered packet prevents older snapshot and approval; current report/snapshot control restores gate. Host lock serializes packet/snapshot/gate and concurrent replay tests pass under race.

prior_findings.assessment: Fresh-token stdout/stderr, exit 9, framed digest, durable reference and over-cap truncation verified after command exit.

prior_findings.title: Go reads case-variant JSON keys that the Python contract ignores
prior_findings.assessment: ASCII and Unicode folded variants cannot override exact fields; receipts and nested JSON use same exact-key decoder.

prior_findings.title: Go and Python disagree on required nonempty report fields
prior_findings.assessment: U+001C..U+001F report rejection preserves blocker; full code-point whitespace parity test passes.

prior_findings.title: Interrupted output-artifact writes are trusted as complete on retry
prior_findings.assessment: Empty, partial and symlink output residues refuse without changing chains/residue; intact artifact reuse succeeds. Publication uses exclusive link after sync.

prior_findings.title: loop-evidence executes a shell command from an imported journal
prior_findings.assessment: Shell, wrappers, forbidden git push/curl/rm argv refuse before execution/appends; direct Capture shell controls refuse.

prior_findings.title: Invalid UTF-8 report passes Go checks but fails the Python validator
prior_findings.assessment: Invalid UTF-8 report, receipt and loop state refuse and preserve blocker/chains.

prior_findings.title: The shell filter refuses a shell name used as plain data
prior_findings.assessment: printf %s sh runs; shell entry points refuse.

prior_findings.title: Executable shell scripts and wrapper aliases bypass the no-shell kernel
prior_findings.assessment: Shell shebang, env shebang, symlink shell interpreter and wrapper aliases refuse in loop and direct Capture. Residual compiled-program behavior is disclosed in code and limitations.

prior_findings.title: A concurrent trusted core terminal append can precede loop check execution
prior_findings.assessment: Independent check nonblockingly probes core and host lock files; both are held. Core Transact spans admission, execution and append.

limitations: This is a fresh audit conversation. No implementer conversation or previous Gate C verdict was supplied or read. Permitted design files/tests contain author commentary and Gate A history; these were treated as artifacts, not as proof. Session isolation is observed locally, not a cryptographic attestation of upstream dispatch.

No optional unblinding occurred. TODO.md contents, scope sections after line 86, prior audit output directories, .serena and Gate D architecture-amendment files were not inspected. Excluded untracked files were hashed only for the requested freeze.

Repository access was operationally read-only and all tests/negative fixtures ran in the external copy. The host workspace itself permits writes; this is not an OS-enforced read-only mount or a separate machine. Tests create and commit only disposable Git fixture repositories.

Genuine worker/model execution and model APIs were forbidden and not used. Receipts are synthetic fixtures shaped against the real ledger interface. Dogfood is explicitly synthetic; no claim of Gate F operational completion is made.

Full Gate D reservation/namespace/generation/lease reconciliation, positive criterion credit, kernel reproduction/budget disposition and full acceptance-contract packet inputs remain human-deferred. Their implementation was not audited as Gate C success.

No-shell checks inspect entry points, symlinks, wrappers and interpreters. Arbitrary compiled programs can spawn a shell internally; this residual is disclosed in noshell.go and requires trusted approved command selection. This report does not claim arbitrary-program sandboxing.
Initial default-TMPDIR test/race runs failed one environment-dependent scratch-directory assertion. Unchanged product code passed with a dedicated scratch TMPDIR; initial failure logs are retained.

Finite tests and static inspection do not prove all possible interleavings. Negative failure cases are reproducible source tests with retained synthetic stores; ordinary passing fixture temporary directories are removed by Go tests.
Jev was unavailable in the host tool inventory. The auditor made bounded audit judgments directly and grants no stage/waiver/release authority.
